problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions of the equation $\operatorname{cos}⁡x=-\frac{7}{9}$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ to the nearest integer?

feedback.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions of the equation $\operatorname{cos}⁡x=-\frac{2}{3}$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ to the nearest integer?
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{2}{3}) & =2.300\,523…≈2.301\end{aligned}
$$

Since $2.301$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=2.301.$

Our first solution lies in the second quadrant and has a reference angle of 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R}=\pi -2.301 & ≈0.841.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=0.841.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14061537/assets/d02a0250df0f0e6c389594ea0e1b119d9f4c63c353553d56c0e865f487862284.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +0.841 \\  & ≈3.983\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
{x}_{1}{x}_{2}≈2.301\cdot 3.983≈9
$$

to the nearest integer.
